title: Composition law for Bernoulli random restrictions
statement:
Fix real parameters $p, q$ with $0 < p \le 1$ and $0 < q \le 1$, and let $E$ be any decidable predicate on the restrictions of $n$ variables. Write $w_p(\rho)$ for the Bernoulli weight of a restriction $\rho$, write $\Pr_p[E]$ for the Bernoulli($p$) probability of $E$, and let $\rho_1 * \rho_2$ denote the composition of $\rho_1$ and $\rho_2$. Then
\[
  \Pr_{pq}[E] \;=\; \sum_{\rho_1} w_p(\rho_1)\,\Pr_q\!\bigl[\,\rho_2 \mapsto E(\rho_1 * \rho_2)\,\bigr],
\]
where the sum runs over all restrictions $\rho_1$ on the $n$ variables, and the inner probability is that of the event that $E$ holds of the composition $\rho_1 * \rho_2$ as $\rho_2$ ranges over a Bernoulli($q$) restriction.
hypotheses_covered: E a decidable predicate on restrictions of n variables
replaced:
For $0 < p \le 1$, $0 < q \le 1$ and any event on restrictions, the Bernoulli($pq$)
probability of the event equals the weighted average, over Bernoulli($p$)
restrictions $\rho_1$, of the Bernoulli($q$) probability that the event holds after
composing with $\rho_1$:
\[
  \mathrm{bernoulliRestrProb}\,(pq)\,\mathrm{event}
  = \sum_{\rho_1} \mathrm{bernoulliRestrWeight}\,p\,\rho_1 \cdot
    \mathrm{bernoulliRestrProb}\,q\,\bigl(\rho_2 \mapsto \mathrm{event}(\mathrm{composeRestr}\,\rho_1\,\rho_2)\bigr).
\]
This says a Bernoulli($p$) restriction followed by a Bernoulli($q$) restriction on
the remaining free variables has the same distribution as a single Bernoulli($pq$)
restriction.
